name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q01 - Total number of sigma bonds in butenyne

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of \(\sigma\) (sigma) bonds present in a molecule of but-1-en-3-yne, \(\mathrm{HC\equiv C-CH=CH_2}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given molecule: but-1-en-3-yne with condensed formula \(\mathrm{HC\equiv C-CH=CH_2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
In covalent bonding, a single bond consists of one \(\sigma\) bond; a double bond consists of one \(\sigma\) bond and one \(\pi\) bond; a triple bond consists of one \(\sigma\) bond and two \(\pi\) bonds. Every carbon-hydrogen (\(\mathrm{C-H}\)) bond is a single \(\sigma\) bond.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total \(\sigma\) bonds = \(\sum \sigma_{\mathrm{C-H}} + \sum \sigma_{\mathrm{C-C}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Counting individual bonds: - Number of \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bonds: one at \(\mathrm{C1}\), one at \(\mathrm{C3}\), and two at \(\mathrm{C4}\), giving \(1 + 1 + 2 = 4\) \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-H}}\) bonds. - Number of \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds: one \(\sigma\) bond in the triple bond \(\mathrm{C1\equiv C2}\), one \(\sigma\) bond in the single bond \(\mathrm{C2-C3}\), and one \(\sigma\) bond in the double bond \(\mathrm{C3=C4}\), giving \(1 + 1 + 1 = 3\) \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-C}}\) bonds. - Total number of \(\sigma\) bonds = \(4 + 3 = 7\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the total atoms: in an acyclic molecule with \(n\) atoms, total \(\sigma\) bonds equal \(n - 1\). Here the formula is \(\mathrm{C_4H_4}\), total atoms = 8. Thus, \(\sigma\) bonds = \(8 - 1 = 7\). The value is verified. The final answer is 7.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q02 - Retardation factor calculation in thin layer chromatography

questiontext.text: In a thin layer chromatography (TLC) experiment, a compound moves a distance of \(3.6\text{ cm}\) from the baseline while the solvent front moves \(9.0\text{ cm}\) from the baseline. Calculate the retardation factor (\(R_f\) value) of the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Distance moved by the substance from baseline, \(x = 3.6\text{ cm}\); distance moved by the solvent front from baseline, \(y = 9.0\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The retardation factor \(R_f\) is a dimensionless ratio defined under uniform chromatographic conditions.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\(R_f = \dfrac{\text{Distance moved by the substance from baseline } (x)}{\text{Distance moved by the solvent from baseline } (y)}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values into the formula: \[R_f = \frac{3.6\text{ cm}}{9.0\text{ cm}} = 0.40\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since the solute travels less than the solvent front, \(R_f\) must be between 0 and 1. The calculated value \(0.40\) lies within this range. The final answer is 0.4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q03 - Total number of pi bonds in hexadienyne

questiontext.text: Determine the total number of \(\pi\) (pi) bonds present in a molecule of hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne, \(\mathrm{CH\equiv C-CH=CH-CH=CH_2}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given molecule: hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne with condensed structural formula \(\mathrm{CH\equiv C-CH=CH-CH=CH_2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
A carbon-carbon single bond contains zero \(\pi\) bonds; a carbon-carbon double bond (\(\mathrm{C=C}\)) contains one \(\sigma\) and one \(\pi\) bond; a carbon-carbon triple bond (\(\mathrm{C\equiv C}\)) contains one \(\sigma\) and two \(\pi\) bonds.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total \(\pi\) bonds = \(\sum \pi_{\mathrm{C=C}} + \sum \pi_{\mathrm{C\equiv C}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Identifying the multiple bonds in the structure: - There is one triple bond at position 5: \(\mathrm{C5\equiv C6}\), which contributes \(2\) \(\pi\) bonds. - There are two double bonds at positions 1 and 3: \(\mathrm{C1=C2}\) and \(\mathrm{C3=C4}\), each contributing \(1\) \(\pi\) bond. - Total number of \(\pi\) bonds = \(2 + 1 + 1 = 4\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verifying by checking the degree of unsaturation (hydrogen deficiency index) for \(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\): for an alkane with 6 carbons, maximum hydrogens = \(2 \times 6 + 2 = 14\). Here, hydrogens = 6. Unsaturation index = \((14 - 6)/2 = 4\). Since the molecule is acyclic, all 4 units of unsaturation are \(\pi\) bonds. The final answer is 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q04 - Number of hyperconjugating hydrogens in carbocation

questiontext.text: Find the number of \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms available for hyperconjugative stabilization in the *tert*-butyl carbocation, \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given species: *tert*-butyl cation, \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+}\), in which three methyl groups are directly attached to the positively charged central carbon.

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Hyperconjugation involves the delocalisation of \(\sigma\) electrons of \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bonds on carbon atoms directly adjacent (\(\alpha\)-position) to the positively charged carbon containing an empty \(2p\) orbital.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total hyperconjugating hydrogens = \(\sum (\text{hydrogens on each attached } \alpha\text{-carbon})\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The central carbon \(\mathrm{C^+}\) is bonded to three equivalent methyl (\(-\mathrm{CH_3}\)) groups. Each methyl group contains \(3\) \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bonds attached to the \(\alpha\)-carbon. Thus, total number of \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms = \(3 \times 3 = 9\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Each of the 9 \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bonds can independently enter into no-bond resonance with the vacant \(2p\) orbital, explaining the high stability of the tertiary carbocation. The final answer is 9.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q05 - Percentage of carbon in organic compound combustion

questiontext.text: During the quantitative estimation of carbon by Liebig's method, complete combustion of \(0.30\text{ g}\) of an organic compound produced \(0.44\text{ g}\) of carbon dioxide. Calculate the mass percentage of carbon in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound taken, \(m = 0.30\text{ g}\); mass of carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO_2}\)) produced, \(m_2 = 0.44\text{ g}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
All carbon present in the organic compound is quantitatively oxidised to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\). Molar mass of \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of carbon = \(12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of carbon = \(\dfrac{12 \times m_2 \times 100}{44 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the measured masses into the expression: \[\text{Percentage of carbon} = \frac{12 \times 0.44\text{ g} \times 100}{44 \times 0.30\text{ g}}\] Simplify the numerator and denominator: \[\frac{12 \times 0.44}{44} = \frac{12 \times 0.01} = 0.12\text{ g of carbon}\] \[\text{Percentage of carbon} = \frac{0.12}{0.30} \times 100 = 40.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated percentage \(40.0\%\) is positive and less than 100%, which is physically consistent. The final answer is 40.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q06 - Percentage of hydrogen from combustion water mass

questiontext.text: In the estimation of hydrogen in an organic compound, complete combustion of \(0.20\text{ g}\) of the substance yielded \(0.18\text{ g}\) of water. Calculate the percentage of hydrogen in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.20\text{ g}\); mass of water (\(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) collected in the calcium chloride tube, \(m_1 = 0.18\text{ g}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
All hydrogen in the organic compound is converted to water. Molar mass of \(\mathrm{H_2O} = 2 \times 1 + 16 = 18\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); mass of two hydrogen atoms in one mole of water = \(2\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of hydrogen = \(\dfrac{2 \times m_1 \times 100}{18 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the values into the formula: \[\text{Percentage of hydrogen} = \frac{2 \times 0.18\text{ g} \times 100}{18 \times 0.20\text{ g}}\] Evaluating intermediate steps: \[\frac{2 \times 0.18}{18} = 0.02\text{ g of hydrogen}\] \[\text{Percentage of hydrogen} = \frac{0.02}{0.20} \times 100 = 10.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the result: \(0.02\text{ g}\) of hydrogen out of \(0.20\text{ g}\) compound is exactly \(1/10\) of the total mass, giving \(10.0\%\). The final answer is 10.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q07 - Percentage of bromine by Carius method estimation

questiontext.text: In Carius method of estimation of halogen, \(0.25\text{ g}\) of an organic bromo compound gave \(0.188\text{ g}\) of silver bromide (\(\mathrm{AgBr}\)). Calculate the percentage of bromine in the compound. (Take atomic masses: \(\mathrm{Ag} = 108\text{ u}\), \(\mathrm{Br} = 80\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.25\text{ g}\); mass of silver bromide (\(\mathrm{AgBr}\)) formed, \(m_1 = 0.188\text{ g}\); atomic masses: \(\mathrm{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{Br} = 80\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{AgBr} = 108 + 80 = 188\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). One mole of \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) (\(188\text{ g}\)) contains one mole of bromine atoms (\(80\text{ g}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of bromine = \(\dfrac{80 \times m_1 \times 100}{188 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given data: \[\text{Percentage of bromine} = \frac{80 \times 0.188\text{ g} \times 100}{188 \times 0.25\text{ g}}\] Notice that \(\dfrac{0.188}{188} = 0.001\text{ mol}\). Mass of bromine in precipitate = \(80 \times 0.001\text{ g} = 0.08\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of bromine} = \frac{0.08}{0.25} \times 100 = 32.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the calculation: \(0.08 / 0.25 = 8/25 = 32/100 = 32.0\%\). Units and magnitude are verified. The final answer is 32.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q08 - Percentage of sulphur in Carius method estimation

questiontext.text: In the estimation of sulphur by Carius method, \(0.16\text{ g}\) of an organic compound afforded \(0.233\text{ g}\) of barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\)). Calculate the percentage of sulphur in the given compound. (Take molar mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 233\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\mathrm{S} = 32\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound taken, \(m = 0.16\text{ g}\); mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) formed, \(m_1 = 0.233\text{ g}\); molar mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 233\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of \(\mathrm{S} = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Sulphur present in the organic compound is oxidised to sulphuric acid and precipitated quantitatively as \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\). Each mole of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) contains one mole of sulphur.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of sulphur = \(\dfrac{32 \times m_1 \times 100}{233 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values: \[\text{Percentage of sulphur} = \frac{32 \times 0.233\text{ g} \times 100}{233 \times 0.16\text{ g}}\] Calculate the mole of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\): \[\frac{0.233}{233} = 0.001\text{ mol}\] Mass of sulphur present = \(32 \times 0.001 = 0.032\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of sulphur} = \frac{0.032\text{ g}}{0.16\text{ g}} \times 100 = 20.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking ratio: \(0.032 / 0.16 = 32 / 160 = 0.20 = 20.0\%\). The percentage is physically plausible. The final answer is 20.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q09 - Percentage of chlorine by Carius tube estimation

questiontext.text: In a Carius estimation of halogen, \(0.20\text{ g}\) of an organic chloro compound gave \(0.287\text{ g}\) of silver chloride (\(\mathrm{AgCl}\)). Find the percentage of chlorine present in the compound. (Take atomic masses: \(\mathrm{Ag} = 108\text{ u}\), \(\mathrm{Cl} = 35.5\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.20\text{ g}\); mass of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) precipitate, \(m_1 = 0.287\text{ g}\); atomic masses: \(\mathrm{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{Cl} = 35.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{AgCl} = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). In \(143.5\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\), there are \(35.5\text{ g}\) of chlorine.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of chlorine = \(\dfrac{35.5 \times m_1 \times 100}{143.5 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the values into the formula: \[\text{Percentage of chlorine} = \frac{35.5 \times 0.287\text{ g} \times 100}{143.5 \times 0.20\text{ g}}\] Evaluate \(\dfrac{0.287}{143.5} = 0.002\text{ mol}\). Mass of chlorine = \(35.5 \times 0.002 = 0.071\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of chlorine} = \frac{0.071}{0.20} \times 100 = 35.5\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verification: \(0.071 / 0.20 = 71 / 200 = 35.5\%\). Units and calculation are verified. The final answer is 35.5.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q10 - Percentage of nitrogen in organic Kjeldahl analysis

questiontext.text: During estimation of nitrogen in an organic compound by Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia evolved from \(0.35\text{ g}\) of the compound neutralized \(10\text{ mL}\) of \(0.5\text{ M } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}\). Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound taken, \(m = 0.35\text{ g}\); volume of sulphuric acid neutralized, \(V = 10\text{ mL}\); molarity of sulphuric acid, \(M = 0.5\text{ M}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The reaction between ammonia and sulphuric acid is: \[2\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \longrightarrow (\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}\] Hence, \(1\text{ mol of } \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \equiv 2\text{ mol of } \mathrm{NH_3} \equiv 2\text{ mol of } \mathrm{N} = 28\text{ g of nitrogen}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of nitrogen = \(\dfrac{1.4 \times M \times 2 \times V}{m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the parameters: \[\text{Moles of } \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \text{ neutralized} = \frac{10 \times 0.5}{1000} = 0.005\text{ mol}\] \[\text{Moles of } \mathrm{NH_3} = 2 \times 0.005 = 0.010\text{ mol}\] \[\text{Mass of nitrogen} = 0.010\text{ mol} \times 14\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.14\text{ g}\] \[\text{Percentage of nitrogen} = \frac{0.14\text{ g}}{0.35\text{ g}} \times 100 = 40.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Using the shortcut formula: \(\dfrac{1.4 \times 0.5 \times 2 \times 10}{0.35} = \dfrac{14}{0.35} = 40.0\%\). Both methods agree. The final answer is 40.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q11 - Count of sp2 hybridized carbons in hydrocarbon

questiontext.text: Determine the number of \(sp^2\) hybridised carbon atoms in a molecule of hepta-1,3-dien-5-yne, \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH=CH-C\equiv C-CH_3}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given compound: hepta-1,3-dien-5-yne with condensed structure \(\mathrm{\overset{1}{C}H_2=\overset{2}{C}H-\overset{3}{C}H=\overset{4}{C}H-\overset{5}{C}\equiv \overset{6}{C}-\overset{7}{C}H_3}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The state of hybridisation of each carbon atom is determined by the number of \(\sigma\) bonds (steric number) it forms: - Carbon forming 4 \(\sigma\) bonds is \(sp^3\) hybridised. - Carbon forming 3 \(\sigma\) bonds (one double bond and two single bonds) is \(sp^2\) hybridised. - Carbon forming 2 \(\sigma\) bonds (one triple bond and one single bond, or two double bonds) is \(sp\) hybridised.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Evaluate the hybridisation state of each of the 7 carbon atoms systematically.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Analysing each carbon atom along the chain: - \(\mathrm{C1}\): forms two \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bonds and one \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bond (total 3 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^2\). - \(\mathrm{C2}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bond and two \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds (total 3 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^2\). - \(\mathrm{C3}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bond and two \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds (total 3 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^2\). - \(\mathrm{C4}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bond and two \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds (total 3 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^2\). - \(\mathrm{C5}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-C}\) single \(\sigma\) bond and one \(\mathrm{C\equiv C}\) \(\sigma\) bond (total 2 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp\). - \(\mathrm{C6}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C\equiv C}\) \(\sigma\) bond and one \(\mathrm{C-C}\) single \(\sigma\) bond (total 2 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp\). - \(\mathrm{C7}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bond and three \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bonds (total 4 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^3\). Thus, carbon atoms 1, 2, 3, and 4 are \(sp^2\) hybridised, giving a total of 4.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Total carbons = 7. Breakdown: 4 \(sp^2\) + 2 \(sp\) + 1 \(sp^3\) = 7. All atoms are accounted for. The final answer is 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q12 - Number of structural chain isomers of pentane

questiontext.text: How many acyclic structural chain isomers are possible for an alkane having the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given molecular formula of saturated acyclic alkane: \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Chain isomers are compounds having the same molecular formula but different carbon skeletons (arrangements of the carbon backbone).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Construct all unique non-cyclic carbon skeleton connectivity networks of 5 carbon atoms.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Identifying the distinct carbon chain arrangements: 1. Unbranched 5-carbon continuous chain: \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}\) (pentane or *n*-pentane). 2. 4-carbon chain with a single one-carbon branch at \(\mathrm{C2}\): \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3}\) (2-methylbutane or isopentane). 3. 3-carbon chain with two one-carbon branches at \(\mathrm{C2}\): \(\mathrm{CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH_3}\) (2,2-dimethylpropane or neopentane). Any other placement is structurally identical due to symmetry. Thus, exactly 3 chain isomers exist.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking IUPAC names: pentane, 2-methylbutane, and 2,2-dimethylpropane are distinct and complete the set of constitutional isomers for \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\). The final answer is 3.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q13 - Percentage of phosphorus in phosphomolybdate precipitation

questiontext.text: In the quantitative analysis of phosphorus, \(0.10\text{ g}\) of an organic compound was heated with fuming nitric acid and then treated with ammonium molybdate. The mass of ammonium phosphomolybdate, \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4\cdot 12MoO_3}\), precipitated was \(0.3754\text{ g}\). Calculate the percentage of phosphorus in the compound. (Take molar mass of \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4\cdot 12MoO_3} = 1877\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\mathrm{P} = 31\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.10\text{ g}\); mass of ammonium phosphomolybdate precipitate, \(m_1 = 0.3754\text{ g}\); molar mass of precipitate = \(1877\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of phosphorus = \(31\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
All phosphorus in the organic compound is converted to phosphoric acid and precipitated as \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4\cdot 12MoO_3}\). Each mole of precipitate contains exactly one mole of phosphorus.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of phosphorus = \(\dfrac{31 \times m_1 \times 100}{1877 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the measured data into the formula: \[\text{Percentage of phosphorus} = \frac{31 \times 0.3754\text{ g} \times 100}{1877 \times 0.10\text{ g}}\] Evaluate \(\dfrac{0.3754}{1877}\): \[\frac{0.3754}{1877} = 0.0002\text{ mol}\] Mass of phosphorus = \(31 \times 0.0002 = 0.0062\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of phosphorus} = \frac{0.0062\text{ g}}{0.10\text{ g}} \times 100 = 6.2\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check: \(0.0062 / 0.10 = 0.062 = 6.2\%\). Units are correct and value is physically reasonable. The final answer is 6.2.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q14 - Number of isomeric aliphatic alcohols of propanol

questiontext.text: How many constitutional (position) isomers of aliphatic alcohols can be represented by the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_3H_8O}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given molecular formula: \(\mathrm{C_3H_8O}\), restricted to aliphatic alcohols (containing the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) functional group).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
In saturated monohydric alcohols of formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}O}\), isomerism arises from differing positions of the hydroxyl group on the carbon skeleton.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
A 3-carbon skeleton allows attachment of the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group at distinct non-equivalent positions.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Examining the propane backbone \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_3}\): 1. Attachment of \(-\mathrm{OH}\) at a terminal carbon (\(\mathrm{C1}\)): \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\) (propan-1-ol). 2. Attachment of \(-\mathrm{OH}\) at the middle secondary carbon (\(\mathrm{C2}\)): \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3}\) (propan-2-ol). Attachment at \(\mathrm{C3}\) is chemically identical to \(\mathrm{C1}\) due to symmetry. Hence, exactly 2 alcohol isomers are possible.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol have molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_3H_8O}\) and represent the complete set of isomeric alcohols. The final answer is 2.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q15 - Percentage of nitrogen via Kjeldahl back titration

questiontext.text: A sample of \(0.50\text{ g}\) of an organic compound was treated according to Kjeldahl's method. The ammonia evolved was absorbed in \(50\text{ mL}\) of \(0.5\text{ M } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}\). The residual acid required \(60\text{ mL}\) of \(0.5\text{ M } \mathrm{NaOH}\) solution for complete neutralisation. Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.50\text{ g}\); initial volume of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\), \(V = 50\text{ mL}\); molarity of acid, \(M = 0.5\text{ M}\); volume of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) used for back-titration, \(V_1 = 60\text{ mL}\); molarity of \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 0.5\text{ M}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Ammonia reacts with sulphuric acid according to: \[2\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \\longrightarrow (\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}\] Unreacted sulphuric acid is neutralised by sodium hydroxide: \[\mathrm{H_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{NaOH} \\longrightarrow \mathrm{Na_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}\] Thus, \(2\text{ moles of } \mathrm{NaOH} \equiv 1\text{ mole of } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Volume of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) of molarity \(M\) unused = \(V - \dfrac{V_1}{2}\). Volume of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) reacted with \(\mathrm{NH_3} = V - \left(V - \dfrac{V_1}{2}\right) = \text{initial} - \text{unused}\). Percentage of nitrogen = \(\dfrac{1.4 \times M \times 2 \left(V - \dfrac{V_1}{2}\right)}{m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculating step-by-step: - Initial millimoles of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = 50\text{ mL} \times 0.5\text{ M} = 25.0\text{ mmol}\). - Millimoles of \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 60\text{ mL} \times 0.5\text{ M} = 30.0\text{ mmol}\). - Unreacted millimoles of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = \dfrac{30.0}{2} = 15.0\text{ mmol}\). - Millimoles of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) consumed by \(\mathrm{NH_3} = 25.0 - 15.0 = 10.0\text{ mmol}\). - Millimoles of \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) evolved = \(2 \times 10.0 = 20.0\text{ mmol}\). - Mass of nitrogen = \(20.0\text{ mmol} \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol mmol}^{-1} \times 14\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.28\text{ g}\). - Percentage of nitrogen = \(\dfrac{0.28\text{ g}}{0.50\text{ g}} \times 100 = 56.0\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking formula directly: \(V - V_1/2 = 50 - 30 = 20\text{ mL}\). \(\text{Percentage of N} = \dfrac{1.4 \times 0.5 \times 2 \times 20}{0.50} = \dfrac{28}{0.50} = 56.0\%\). Both methods yield identical results. The final answer is 56.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q16 - Nitrogen estimation by Dumas method aqueous tension

questiontext.text: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen, \(0.30\text{ g}\) of an organic compound gave \(50.0\text{ mL}\) of nitrogen gas collected over aqueous \(\mathrm{KOH}\) at \(300\text{ K}\) and \(715\text{ mm Hg}\) pressure. If the aqueous tension at \(300\text{ K}\) is \(15\text{ mm Hg}\), calculate the percentage of nitrogen in the compound. (Give answer to two decimal places).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.30\text{ g}\); volume of nitrogen collected, \(V_1 = 50.0\text{ mL}\); temperature, \(T_1 = 300\text{ K}\); barometric pressure = \(715\text{ mm Hg}\); aqueous tension = \(15\text{ mm Hg}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The pressure of dry nitrogen gas is obtained by subtracting the aqueous tension of water from the barometric pressure. Standard temperature is \(T_0 = 273\text{ K}\) and standard pressure is \(P_0 = 760\text{ mm Hg}\). Under STP, \(22400\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) weighs \(28\text{ g}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Actual pressure of dry nitrogen: \(p_1 = \text{Atmospheric pressure} - \text{Aqueous tension}\). Volume of dry nitrogen at STP: \(V = \dfrac{p_1 \times V_1 \times 273}{760 \times T_1}\). Percentage of nitrogen: \(\text{Percentage of N} = \dfrac{28 \times V \times 100}{22400 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Executing calculations step by step: 1. \(p_1 = 715 - 15 = 700\text{ mm Hg}\). 2. \(V = \dfrac{700 \times 50.0 \times 273}{760 \times 300} = \dfrac{9555000}{228000} \approx 41.908\text{ mL}\). 3. Mass of \(41.908\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) at STP: \(\dfrac{28 \times 41.908}{22400} \approx 0.052385\text{ g}\). 4. \(\text{Percentage of nitrogen} = \dfrac{0.052385}{0.30} \times 100 \approx 17.46\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(p_1\) in \(\text{mm Hg}\), \(V\) in \(\text{mL}\), mass in \(\text{g}\). The calculated value \(17.46\%\) exactly matches the standard textbook solution. The final answer is 17.46.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q17 - Percentage of oxygen from carbon dioxide estimation

questiontext.text: In the direct estimation of oxygen, an organic compound is decomposed in a stream of nitrogen. The liberated oxygen is converted to \(\mathrm{CO}\) over red-hot coke and subsequently oxidised to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) by \(\mathrm{I_2O_5}\). If \(0.20\text{ g}\) of the organic compound produces \(0.22\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), calculate the percentage of oxygen in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound taken, \(m = 0.20\text{ g}\); mass of carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO_2}\)) produced, \(m_1 = 0.22\text{ g}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The chemical transformations are: \[2\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \xrightarrow{1373\text{ K}} 2\mathrm{CO}\] \[\mathrm{I_2O_5} + 5\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow \mathrm{I_2} + 5\mathrm{CO_2}\] Multiplying the first equation by 5 and the second by 2 gives: \[5\mathrm{O_2} \equiv 10\mathrm{CO} \equiv 10\mathrm{CO_2}\] Hence, \(1\text{ mol of } \mathrm{O_2}\) (\(32\text{ g}\)) produces \(2\text{ mol of } \mathrm{CO_2}\) (\(2 \times 44 = 88\text{ g}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of oxygen = \(\dfrac{32 \times m_1 \times 100}{88 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values: \[\text{Percentage of oxygen} = \frac{32 \times 0.22\text{ g} \times 100}{88 \times 0.20\text{ g}}\] Simplify algebraically: \[\frac{0.22}{88} = \frac{1}{400} = 0.0025\text{ mol of } \mathrm{O_2}\] \[\text{Mass of oxygen} = \frac{32 \times 0.22}{88} = 0.08\text{ g}\] \[\text{Percentage of oxygen} = \frac{0.08\text{ g}}{0.20\text{ g}} \times 100 = 40.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the ratio: \(0.08 / 0.20 = 8/20 = 40.0\%\). The stoichiometry and calculations are consistent with the textbook derivation. The final answer is 40.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q18 - Mass of carbon dioxide from combustion percentage

questiontext.text: An organic compound contains \(69.0\%\) carbon and \(4.8\%\) hydrogen, the remainder being oxygen. Calculate the mass of carbon dioxide (in grams) produced when \(0.20\text{ g}\) of this substance is subjected to complete combustion.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.20\text{ g}\); percentage of carbon in compound = \(69.0\%\); molar mass of \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 44\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of carbon = \(12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
During combustion, all carbon in the sample is converted into carbon dioxide. The mass of carbon dioxide produced, \(m_2\), is directly related to the mass of carbon present.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\(\text{Percentage of carbon} = \dfrac{12 \times m_2 \times 100}{44 \times m}\). Rearranging for \(m_2\): \[m_2 = \frac{\text{Percentage of carbon} \times 44 \times m}{12 \times 100}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given numerical values: \[m_2 = \frac{69.0 \times 44 \times 0.20\text{ g}}{1200}\] Calculate intermediate products: - Numerator: \(69.0 \times 44 \times 0.20 = 607.2\). - Division: \(m_2 = \dfrac{607.2}{1200} = 0.506\text{ g}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the mass of carbon: \(0.20 \times 0.69 = 0.138\text{ g}\) of C. Mass of \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 0.138 \times (44/12) = 0.138 \times 3.6667 = 0.506\text{ g}\). The calculation is verified. The final answer is 0.506.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q19 - Phosphorus estimation via magnesium pyrophosphate precipitate

questiontext.text: In the estimation of phosphorus, \(0.31\text{ g}\) of an organic compound was oxidized to phosphoric acid and precipitated as \(\mathrm{MgNH_4PO_4}\), which on ignition yielded \(0.222\text{ g}\) of magnesium pyrophosphate (\(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}\)). Calculate the percentage of phosphorus in the compound. (Take molar mass of \(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7} = 222\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\mathrm{P} = 31\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.31\text{ g}\); mass of \(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}\) residue after ignition, \(m_1 = 0.222\text{ g}\); molar mass of \(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7} = 222\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); mass of two phosphorus atoms = \(2 \times 31 = 62\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Each mole of magnesium pyrophosphate (\(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}\)) contains two moles of phosphorus atoms. Thus, \(222\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}\) contains \(62\text{ g}\) of phosphorus.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of phosphorus = \(\dfrac{62 \times m_1 \times 100}{222 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values: \[\text{Percentage of phosphorus} = \frac{62 \times 0.222\text{ g} \times 100}{222 \times 0.31\text{ g}}\] Notice that \(\dfrac{0.222}{222} = 0.001\text{ mol}\). Mass of phosphorus in the residue = \(62 \times 0.001 = 0.062\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of phosphorus} = \frac{0.062\text{ g}}{0.31\text{ g}} \times 100 = 20.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking ratio: \(0.062 / 0.31 = 62 / 310 = 1/5 = 0.20 = 20.0\%\). Result is verified. The final answer is 20.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q20 - Percentage of sulphur in organic Carius analysis

questiontext.text: In the estimation of sulphur by Carius method, \(0.468\text{ g}\) of an organic sulphur compound afforded \(0.668\text{ g}\) of barium sulphate. Find the percentage of sulphur in the given compound. (Take molar mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 233\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\mathrm{S} = 32\text{ u}\). Give answer to two decimal places).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic sulphur compound, \(m = 0.468\text{ g}\); mass of barium sulphate formed, \(m_1 = 0.668\text{ g}\); molar mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 233\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of sulphur = \(32\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Sulphur is converted quantitatively to sulphate and precipitated as barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\)). One mole of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) (\(233\text{ g}\)) contains one mole of sulphur (\(32\text{ g}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of sulphur = \(\dfrac{32 \times m_1 \times 100}{233 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the numerical values into the formula: \[\text{Percentage of sulphur} = \frac{32 \times 0.668\text{ g} \times 100}{233 \times 0.468\text{ g}}\] Evaluate numerator and denominator: - Numerator: \(32 \times 0.668 \times 100 = 2137.6\). - Denominator: \(233 \times 0.468 = 109.044\). - Ratio: \(\dfrac{2137.6}{109.044} \approx 19.6029\% \approx 19.60\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the intermediate mass of sulphur: \(\dfrac{32 \times 0.668}{233} \approx 0.09174\text{ g}\). Fraction: \(\dfrac{0.09174}{0.468} \times 100 \approx 19.60\%\). The answer is verified to two decimal places. The final answer is 19.60.
